audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phases[0..6].side all read 'Skill' while the content layer reads Irelia on all seven rows — a cross-layer disagreement on every stage. Separately, the whole chart contradicts the rest of the page: diff is TRICKY 7/10 with Galio carry threat 7.5/10 and the Emerald+ win rate is 44.45% over 1145 games, yet the chart hands Irelia 7 stages out of 7. packet.defects flags exactly this.
audit.why: packet.levelChart agrees with the content layer, so it is the tiebreak for the layer disagreement. It does not resolve the chart-vs-win-rate contradiction, which I could not settle from the kit alone.
audit.corrected: Full-layer sides moved onto the content values so the two layers stop arguing. The chart-vs-win-rate contradiction is raised as a question rather than guessed at.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike claimed 'your dash-and-knockup engage'. Irelia has no knockup — Galio does, via Justice Punch and Hero's Entrance.
audit.why: Irelia's R Marks and leaves a slowing wall. Hero's Entrance is 180/160/140s and shields allies before it lands.
audit.corrected: Knockup attributed to Galio; the 180s cooldown stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: The lane's decisive interaction was absent and two abilities were mis-slotted: early called Winds of War 'his W poke' (W is Shield of Durand), mid called the taunt 'his taunt (E)' (E is Justice Punch), and wants.you[1] invented a passive called 'Colossal Consciousness'.
audit.why: Shield of Durand is a 275-range charged stance on 18/17/16/15/14s that shields him AND taunts on release — a taunt is the single hardest counter to a dash-reset pattern, because it eats the commit outright. Justice Punch is an 11/10/9/8/7s 650-range dash that knocks up. Winds of War is an 11s 825-range DoT zone. The real passive is Colossal Smash, an auto-attack reset whose wind-up is the burst tell.
audit.corrected: Correct slots, the taunt named as the thing that flips the all-in, and Colossal Smash's reset written into wants.you[1] and the do's.

audit.why: Justice Punch 11s->7s, Shield of Durand 18s->14s, Winds of War 11s->7s, Hero's Entrance 180s.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim; dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim, both under unrelated titles.

edits.before: W joins: the channel shreds incoming damage — hold it for his trade spell, not his autos.
edits.after: W joins, but Defiant Dance cuts physical only — Galio's damage is magic, so it does little.

edits.before: Reset-dance the wave into his face: four stacks, E-stun, Q the kill threat. The lane is a minion-count quiz.
edits.after: Reset-dance the wave into his face: four stacks, E-stun, Q the kill threat — but never into a charged W.

edits.before: Q-reset through two low minions onto his chest, four-stack autos, E-stun the retreat — the wave-funded all-in he budgeted zero for.
edits.after: Q-reset through two low minions onto his chest, four stacks, E-stun the retreat — go while Shield of Durand is down.

edits.before: Good trade: Q-reset through two low minions onto his chest, four-stack autos, E-stun the retreat — the wave-funded all-in he budgeted zero for. Bad trade: Dashing in under-stacked with W down — Irelia without the engine is a melee minion with a famous haircut.
edits.after: Good trade: Q-reset through two low minions onto his chest, four stacks, E-stun the retreat — go while Shield of Durand is down. Bad trade: Dashing in under-stacked with W down — Irelia without the engine is a melee minion with a famous haircut.

edits.before: His dash knockup — he has no engage while it is down. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Justice Punch is an 11s dash that knocks you up — he has no engage without it, so move on its downtime.

edits.before: Q-reset through two low minions onto his chest, four-stack autos, E-stun the retreat — the wave-funded all-in he budgeted zero for.
edits.after: Colossal Smash is an auto-reset every few seconds — the swing wind-up is the tell, so save Defiant Dance for the charged taunt.

edits.before: Dashing in under-stacked with W down — Irelia without the engine is a melee minion with a famous haircut.
edits.after: Blades converging along his walking line are a free dodge, and a whiffed E leaves you in Winds of War with no stun.

edits.before: - Galio Justice Punch: matchup-defining — His dash knockup — he has no engage while it is down. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget W Defiant Dance for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Justice Punch is 11s at rank 1, 7s maxed — his only engage, so move on its downtime. - Shield of Durand taunts at 275 range on 18s and shields him the whole charge. - Winds of War is 11s, Hero's Entrance 180s.

edits.before: Galio wins by landing Justice Punch, denying your pattern, and turning your every misstep into the all-in you hadn’t budgeted.
edits.after: Galio wins by chipping you inside Winds of War, taunting your commit with Shield of Durand, and knocking you out of the reset.

edits.before: If Galio gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Justice Punch extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with Q resets and stay relevant through stacked windows.
edits.after: If Galio gets a kill, stop dashing into the 275-range taunt — Shield of Durand turns your all-in into his. Farm what Bladesurge can reach, and step up only when Justice Punch and the shield are both spent.

edits.before: Carry through the dance — the wave funds dives no cooldown can, and your R turns skirmishes into no-exit interviews.
edits.after: Carry on his downtime: with Justice Punch and the taunt both spent, he owns nothing that stops the reset chain.

edits.before: You are the front-to-back blender: Q through their line, stun the carries, and let the marks ground the peel.
edits.after: You are the front-to-back blender: Q through their line, E-stun the carries, and let R's wall slow whoever peels.

edits.before: Ahead, dance louder: crash waves into Galio's face, stun the answers, and surf resets through every river fight.
edits.after: Ahead, punish the stance: charging Shield of Durand slows him, so step in as it drops and take the plates.

edits.before: Best wave: a slow push of low-HP minions — every one is a dash and the crash is an all-in announcement you control. Worst wave: a crashed wave and an empty lane — no minions, no dashes, no Irelia. Crash timing: shove with a destination in mind; mid waves are bus tickets, not chores.
edits.after: Best wave: a slow push of low-HP minions between you and him — each is a Bladesurge and the crash is an all-in you control. Worst wave: a crashed wave and an empty lane, where Winds of War chips you from 825 and nothing is left to dash to. Crash timing: crash while Justice Punch is down; mid waves are bus tickets, not chores.

edits.before: His telegraphed poke and shield cooldown keep him reactive at level 2 while you close distance freely
edits.after: Winds of War is his only level 2 damage and Shield of Durand is 18s, so you still close distance freely

edits.before: Hero's Entrance is a roam tool rather than a duel cooldown, so level 6 changes nothing about your 1v1 advantage
edits.after: Hero's Entrance is a 180s map tool rather than a duel cooldown, so level 6 changes little in a straight 1v1

edits.before: Galio's Winds of War needs to be angled well to hit and his Shield of Durand is his only real damage mitigation, so a level 3 all-in the moment his shield is down punishes him hard.
edits.after: Winds of War is an 11s zone he has to angle, and Shield of Durand both shields and taunts on an 18s cooldown, so a level 3 all-in the moment that shield is down punishes him hard.

edits.before: Hero's Entrance is a team-fight roam tool, not a lane dueling ability, so at level 6 he still has no answer to your dash-and-knockup engage in a 1v1.
edits.after: Hero's Entrance is a 180s team-fight tool, not a lane dueling ability, so at level 6 he answers your dash with Justice Punch and nothing more.

edits.before: Galio is built as a durable teamfight tool, not a lane bully, and his kit has almost nothing to punish your melee aggression pre-6. His W poke is telegraphed and his shield has a real cooldown — walk up and all-in the moment it's down, since he lacks the burst to punish your engage. Push the wave hard through levels 1-5; he simply doesn't have the damage to threaten you in a straight fight.
edits.after: Galio is built as a durable teamfight tool, not a lane bully, but his kit is not empty: Winds of War chips you from 825 and Shield of Durand taunts at 275 range while shielding him. Walk up and all-in the moment that 18s shield is down, and never dash into a charged stance. Push the wave through levels 1-5; his damage alone doesn't beat you in a straight fight, but the taunt does if you feed it one.

edits.before: His ultimate Hero's Entrance is built for roaming to teamfights, not for winning a lane duel, so hitting 6 changes almost nothing about your 1v1 matchup. Keep initiating fights whenever his shield or W are down; his taunt (E) is his only real disruption tool and it doesn't do enough damage to flip an all-in on its own. Watch for him using his ultimate to set up plays elsewhere on the map — that's when you should shove and roam yourself.
edits.after: Hero's Entrance is built for roaming to teamfights on a 180s cooldown, not for winning a lane duel, so hitting 6 changes little about the 1v1. Keep initiating whenever Shield of Durand or Justice Punch are down; the taunt is his real disruption tool and it flips an all-in the instant you dash into the charge. Watch for him ulting to set up plays elsewhere on the map — that's when you shove and roam yourself.

edits.before: Even with a full tank build, Galio's damage output stays low relative to your scaling all-in — he's built to peel and engage for teammates, not to win extended 1v1 trades. Keep forcing fights when you catch him without support nearby; his taunt is disruptive but not lethal, and your dive kit still closes these fights out.
edits.after: Even with a full tank build, Galio's damage output stays low relative to your scaling all-in — he's built to peel and engage for teammates, not to win extended 1v1 trades. Keep forcing fights when you catch him without support nearby; the taunt is the disruption that actually matters, so bait Shield of Durand before you spend the reset chain.

edits.before: Deny his passive Colossal Consciousness stacking by trading efficiently
edits.after: Step back on the Colossal Smash wind-up — his passive is an auto-reset

notes: 'Colossal Consciousness' was a fabricated ability name in wants.you[1]; the passive is Colossal Smash. Two ability slots were also swapped in prose (Winds of War called 'his W poke', Justice Punch called 'his taunt (E)'). The taunt — Shield of Durand, 275 range, 18s — was nowhere on the page despite being the interaction that decides a dash-reset matchup; it is now stated in early, mid, late, feeding and the trading line. I did NOT flip any chart row: see questionsForUser.
